question.label: The question
question.title: Revenue rests on first orders

body.template: Olist connects small Brazilian sellers to customers through one storefront. Between January 2017 and August 2018 it delivered {delivered} orders to {customers} customers, and only {repeat} of them came back on a later day.
With {opc} orders per customer, revenue depends almost entirely on finding new buyers. This case asks what stands between a first order and a second one, and what the marketplace could change.

question.tree_note: Factors are rounded, so their product is close to, not exactly, the revenue.

why.template: Second and later orders bring in only {share} of revenue, so bringing past buyers back is largely untapped.
Orders handed over after the seller's deadline run late {late} of the time against {ontime}, and handover is the step sellers control.
{before} of late orders are rated before they arrive, so many low scores are given while the parcel is still on its way.

F4.title: A few sellers carry the marketplace

why.template: {sellers} sellers account for {share} of scorecard late handovers, so a handover standard can start with a small group.

F5.title: Growth came from volume, not bigger baskets

why.template: Freight adds {q1} to the cheapest quarter of orders, which makes free freight a meaningful incentive to test.
